task: A user reports the whole process aborts with a fatal CHECK failure in StringBytes::StorageSize when they write a hex string with an odd number of characters to an HTTP request. Writing the same string with a single socket write does not crash. What is going on and how should it be fixed?
gold: HTTP requests are corked so the write goes through Writev, which calls StringBytes::StorageSize, whose CHECK fatal-asserted on odd-length hex; a single Write goes through HexDecode, which silently drops the trailing incomplete nibble
Fix: remove the CHECK in StorageSize (src/string_bytes.cc) and let integer division handle odd lengths, consistent with StringBytes::Size and HexDecode

task: A WritableStream obtained from Writable.toWeb() stops making progress forever after the first backpressured write. It mostly happens when the underlying Node Writable has highWaterMark: 0. Why?
gold: The underlying Writable can emit 'drain' synchronously during write(), before the adapter starts waiting for it, so the adapter waits for an event that already happened
Fix in the webstreams adapter (lib/internal/webstreams/adapters.js): check writableNeedDrain right after a backpressured write and resolve the backpressure promise if the stream has already drained

task: Building a zip archive with the zip API hangs forever when one of the listed source paths is a named pipe (FIFO), and afterwards other fs work seems to stall too. The code already rejects non-regular files, so how does this happen?
gold: zipFiles() opened each source before fstat-ing it, so open() on a FIFO or slow device blocks indefinitely; the regular-file guard (fstat) runs too late
Each stuck open pins a libuv threadpool thread, which starves other fs work
Fix: open with O_NONBLOCK (in lib/internal/zip/archive.js) so the open returns promptly and fstat can reject the non-regular file; O_NONBLOCK has no effect on regular-file reads

task: An embedder compiles Node.js with -std=c++23 and the process hangs in the very first foreground task flush. With Node's normal build flags it works. What causes this?
gold: The platform code drained queues with `for (auto& task : queue.Lock().PopAll())`; C++23 (P2718R0) extends the lifetime of temporaries in a range-for initializer to the end of the loop, so the queue mutex stays held while tasks run (in C++20 the Locked temporary died before the body)
The first task that posts to the same queue deadlocks on the non-recursive mutex
Fix: store the drained tasks in a local vector before iterating (FlushForegroundTasksInternal and DelayedTaskScheduler in src/node_platform.cc), so the lock is released regardless of language version

task: Streams created from a FileHandle with autoClose: false leak a 'close' listener on the handle each time. I want to fix it in importFd by removing the listener and calling the handle's kUnref on the stream's end/finish/error. Good idea?
gold: That exact fix was merged (fs: fix close listener leak in FileHandle streams) and then reverted
It was reverted because it was judged broken: it can unref the handle multiple times

task: To cut CI cost I'd like to move our dependency-update GitHub Actions workflows (tools updates, OpenSSL update, timezone update) onto the ubuntu-slim runner. Anything to watch out for?
gold: This was tried and reverted back to ubuntu-latest for those workflows
The tools workflow's undici update script and the OpenSSL update workflow require Docker, which ubuntu-slim does not have
The timezone update script needs icupkg, which is not available on ubuntu-slim

task: Should AbortSignal emit the usual MaxListenersExceededWarning (possible memory leak) by default when many listeners are added, like other EventTargets do?
gold: No: the default kMaxEventTargetListeners for AbortSignal was deliberately set to 0, disabling the leak warning by default
Reason: so users can write isomorphic library code (lots of listeners on one signal is a normal pattern)
It can still be enabled per AbortSignal instance with setMaxListeners

task: On AIX, fs.rmSync on a directory we lack permission to delete throws something other than a clean permission error. Is this a known platform issue, and how does Node handle it?
gold: On AIX the clang libc++ std::filesystem::remove_all() returns EEXIST instead of EACCES when lacking permission to remove a directory recursively
RmSync in src/node_file.cc has an #ifdef _AIX branch that treats file_exists as well as permission_denied as the permission-denied case, throwing the 'Permission denied' error

task: At startup Node seeds V8's entropy (hash seeds, ASLR, Math.random) from the OS CSPRNG via uv_random() rather than OpenSSL. Why is AIX treated differently here?
gold: On AIX uv_random() reads the blocking /dev/random
So AIX stays on OpenSSL's DRBG (which seeds from /dev/urandom) for V8's entropy

task: What is the default Buffer.poolSize, and which Buffer allocations are served from the shared pool?
gold: The default Buffer.poolSize is 64 KiB (65536)
Only allocations smaller than half the pool size (size < Buffer.poolSize >>> 1, i.e. under 32 KiB) use the pool, via allocUnsafe/from etc.; larger ones get their own allocation
